ICD-10-CM code(s): B20 Human immunodeficiency virus [HIV] disease (Z21 asymptomatic HIV: not in data)
Source(s): HHS/NIH Adult & Adolescent ARV Guidelines; INSIGHT START Study Group, NEJM 2015
Notes: All 41 are on an ARV. Emtricitabine/tenofovir is also PrEP for HIV-negative people, so identify by B20, not by drug.

ICD-10-CM code(s): Z94 Transplanted organ and tissue status (Z94.0 kidney); T86 Complications of transplanted organs (only T86.9P 'Prevent transplanted organ and tissue rejection')
Life-saving drug(s): Tacrolimus, mycophenolate, oral cyclosporine, sirolimus/everolimus, azathioprine
Source(s): KDIGO 2009 Kidney Transplant Recipient Guideline; Butler et al., Transplantation 2004
Notes: Appears almost entirely as the P code T86.9P, so the P column is the real transplant count. P-code share = 0.093% (~0.88M Americans). Same drugs also used for lupus/RA/IBD.

ICD-10-CM code(s): E10 Type 1 diabetes mellitus (E10, E10.2, E10.4)
Source(s): ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes
Notes: 40/41 on insulin. Insulin alone is not specific (most insulin users are E11), so define by E10. Some T1D may self-report as E11.

ICD-10-CM code(s): I48 Atrial fibrillation and flutter (I48.9, I48.91, I48.92)
Life-saving drug(s): Oral anticoagulants: warfarin, apixaban, rivaroxaban, dabigatran, edoxaban
Source(s): 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF Guideline (Joglar et al., Circulation 2024); Hart, Pearce & Aguilar, Ann Intern Med 2007
Notes: Only 90/201 are on an OAC (rest on rate control). Many OAC users instead report D75.9P 'Prevent blood clots' (456 people, 1.4%), which is shared with VTE/valves, so AF-specific anticoagulation is undercounted.

ICD-10-CM code(s): I26 Pulmonary embolism; I80 Phlebitis and thrombophlebitis (I80.3); I82 Other venous embolism/thrombosis: not in data
Life-saving drug(s): Anticoagulants: apixaban, rivaroxaban, warfarin, dabigatran, enoxaparin
Source(s): Barritt & Jordan, Lancet 1960; Stevens et al., CHEST VTE Guideline 2021
Notes: I26 = 25 people, I80 = 71; 6 overlap, so 90 unique. 62/90 on an anticoagulant. Generic P code D75.9P 'Prevent blood clots' (456 people) likely holds many VTE patients but cannot be split from AF.

Condition: Cardiac/vascular implant (prosthetic heart valve, stent, bypass, pacemaker)
ICD-10-CM code(s): Z95 Presence of cardiac and vascular implants and grafts (Z95, Z95.0 pacemaker, Z95.1 CABG, Z95.2 prosthetic heart valve, Z95.5 coronary stent, Z95.9)
Source(s): 2020 ACC/AHA Valvular Heart Disease Guideline (Otto et al., Circulation 2021); 2016 ACC/AHA DAPT Focused Update (Levine et al., JACC)
Notes: At 3 characters Z95 lumps valves, stents, bypass and pacemakers; 2015+ coding is mostly bare 'Z95' (23 of 39). Only Z95.2 (7 people, all on warfarin) is the mechanical-valve case.

ICD-10-CM code(s): I21 Acute myocardial infarction (STEMI/NSTEMI); I25 Chronic ischemic heart disease (I25.9); P: I21.P Prevent heart attack
Life-saving drug(s): P2Y12 inhibitors (clopidogrel, ticagrelor, prasugrel) + aspirin after MI/stent
Source(s): 2016 ACC/AHA DAPT Focused Update (Levine et al., JACC 2016)
Notes: I21 = 57, I25 = 7, 64 unique. 33/64 on a P2Y12. P code I21.P is huge (P-code share = 1.411% (~13.40M Americans)) but only 70 of 498 are on a P2Y12; most are aspirin/statin primary prevention, so P here mostly is not 'has the condition'.

ICD-10-CM code(s): I50 Heart failure (I50.9)
Source(s): PARADIGM-HF (McMurray et al., NEJM 2014); 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA HF Guideline
Notes: Only 8/312 take sacubitril/valsartan; other HF drugs are shared with hypertension/diabetes. Fits 'has condition' well, fits 'unique drug' poorly.

ICD-10-CM code(s): C50 Malignant neoplasm of breast; P: C50.P Prevent breast cancer (split across 'Prevent breast cancer' 13 and typo 'Prevent barest cancer' 17)
Source(s): EBCTCG, Lancet 2011 (tamoxifen); EBCTCG, Lancet 2015 (aromatase inhibitors)
Notes: 51/56 on one of these drugs. P-code share = 0.112% (~1.06M Americans). Many C50.P people are probably survivors on adjuvant therapy who said 'prevent', so P may belong with the treated group here.

ICD-10-CM code(s): C61 Malignant neoplasm of prostate; P: C61.P Prevent prostate cancer
Source(s): LATITUDE (Fizazi et al., NEJM 2017); ENZAMET (Davis et al., NEJM 2019)
Notes: 16/24 on an oral antiandrogen. Life-saving mainly in metastatic disease. Injected ADT may be missed. P-code share = 0.002%.

ICD-10-CM code(s): C92 Myeloid leukemia: NOT in data (TKI users are coded C95.9 leukemia unspecified, C96.9, C80.1P)
Source(s): IRIS 10-year follow-up (Hochhaus et al., NEJM 2017)
Notes: Not findable by code; only 5 TKI users since 2013. Drop.

ICD-10-CM code(s): G40 Epilepsy and recurrent seizures; R56 Convulsions (R56.9); P: G40.P Prevent seizures
Life-saving drug(s): Levetiracetam, phenytoin, lacosamide, oxcarbazepine, carbamazepine, lamotrigine, valproate
Source(s): RANSOM study (Faught et al., Neurology 2008)
Notes: G40 = 247, R56 = 1. 220/248 on an antiseizure drug. Levetiracetam/phenytoin/lacosamide are seizure-specific; lamotrigine, valproate, topiramate, gabapentin are not. P-code share = 0.004%.

ICD-10-CM code(s): E27 Other disorders of adrenal gland (E27.1 primary adrenocortical insufficiency, E27.40, E27.9 unspecified); E23 Hypofunction of pituitary: not in data
Source(s): Endocrine Society Primary Adrenal Insufficiency Guideline (Bornstein et al., JCEM 2016)
Notes: 9/11 on hydrocortisone/fludrocortisone. E27.9 (8 of 11) is 'adrenal disorder unspecified', so some may not be insufficiency. Exclude topical/otic hydrocortisone.

ICD-10-CM code(s): G70 Myasthenia gravis: NOT in data (5 pyridostigmine users coded 55555/99999/M62.81)
Source(s): International Consensus Guidance for MG 2020 Update (Narayanaswami et al., Neurology 2021)
Notes: Not findable by code. Drop.

ICD-10-CM code(s): I27 Other pulmonary heart diseases (only I27.9 unspecified)
Life-saving drug(s): Bosentan, ambrisentan, macitentan, riociguat, treprostinil, selexipag; sildenafil/tadalafil
Source(s): NIH Registry (D'Alonzo et al., Ann Intern Med 1991); 2022 ESC/ERS PH Guidelines
Notes: 4/9 on a PAH-specific drug (ERA/riociguat/treprostinil). I27.9 does not separate PAH (group 1) from other pulmonary hypertension.

ICD-10-CM code(s): B19 Unspecified viral hepatitis (B19, B19.1 hepatitis B unspecified). B16 acute hep B: not in data. B18 chronic viral hepatitis is present (3 people) but all are B18.2 = hepatitis C, so excluded
Source(s): AASLD 2018 Hepatitis B Guidance (Terrault et al., Hepatology 2018)
Notes: Only 1 person explicitly hep B; 5 of 11 B19 people are on entecavir (HBV-only drug). Weak; consider defining as 'B19 + entecavir'.

ICD-10-CM code(s): E84 Cystic fibrosis: NOT in data (pancrelipase users coded K86/K87 pancreatic disease)
Source(s): Middleton et al., NEJM 2019; CF Foundation Patient Registry
Notes: Not findable by code. Drop.

ICD-10-CM code(s): F11 Opioid related disorders (F11.2 opioid dependence, F11.23 with withdrawal)
Source(s): Sordo et al., BMJ 2017; Larochelle et al., Ann Intern Med 2018
Notes: All 29 on MOUD. Methadone/buprenorphine are also prescribed for pain; clinic-dispensed methadone may be under-reported.

ICD-10-CM code(s): Z91 Personal risk factors (Z91.01 food allergy status, Z91.030 bee allergy status). T78 is present (508 people) but is entirely T78.40 'Allergy, unspecified' = antihistamine users, so excluded
Source(s): Anaphylaxis 2020 Practice Parameter Update (Shaker et al., JACI 2020)
Notes: Only 3 people, none on epinephrine. Rescue med not captured well by a 30-day prescription survey. Drop.

ICD-10-CM code(s): F31 Bipolar disorder (F31.9)
Source(s): Cipriani et al., BMJ 2013
Notes: Only 20/195 on lithium; other bipolar drugs are non-specific. Mortality pathway is suicide.
